lens: F6_Better_Alternative — What's the better way? Why not that way? If 'later', bounded FixupTask with priority + reasoning? At least one Linus-style and one hyperscaler-style alternative per load-bearing decision?
answer: PASS_WITH_RESERVATIONS. v4 §A.3 enumerates 4 supervisor-topology options (A/B/C/D) and chooses D with explicit cost-benefit rejection of each — this satisfies F6 multi-alternative requirement for the topology decision. v5 §A.1 enumerates 2 renderer options (per-provider adapters vs multi-format dispatch) with verdicts — but TWO is the floor for CC-1 deep, not the bar. Three load-bearing decisions ship WITHOUT an explicit options table: (1) inbox storage substrate (JSONL on disk vs SQLite/sled/redb/lmdb/NATS-JetStream/Kafka-on-disk); (2) supervisor↔CLI notification mechanism (100ms file-existence polling vs inotify/kqueue/fsevents vs Unix-domain-socket vs MCP push vs DAP-style protocol vs signalfd); (3) settings-template language (hand-rolled TOML vs Dhall/CUE/jsonnet/Nickel vs build.rs-codegen-from-schema). Each of these is a first-solution-wins selection where the rejected alternatives are not named, even though the Linus-style answer (SQLite for inbox; inotify for stop-notify) and hyperscaler-style answer (NATS JetStream; gRPC streaming) would clearly compete on principled grounds. The Branch Y dep-commitment is named as a principle in §A.1 but the Branch-X/Branch-Z hybrid alternatives that v3 reportedly considered are not preserved in the v4/v5 artifact — F6 cannot verify the rejection was deliberate vs inherited.
key_claims: Supervisor topology (v4 §A.3) — 4 options enumerated (A=single daemon, B=per-CLI binaries, C=in-process dashboard, D=host-injected ports); D chosen; A/C rejected on principle; B rejected on cost-benefit at current throughput. THIS DECISION SATISFIES F6.

Settings renderer (v5 §A.1) — 2 options enumerated (A=per-provider adapters, B=multi-format dispatch with format-flag); A chosen as it mirrors v4 driver-not-kernel layering. ONLY 2 options for a CC-1 deep change is below F6's recommended 3+ floor.

Inbox storage (v4 §B.2.4) — JSONL chosen with hand-rolled framing; ZERO explicit alternatives table. SQLite (single-file ACID, fsync handled), sled/redb (embedded Rust KV), NATS JetStream / Kafka-on-disk (push delivery, native dedup), lmdb (mmap-fast), or even an append-only segment log (BitCask-style) are all viable competitors that don't appear in §A.3 or §B.2.4.

Stop-hook notification (v4 §B.3) — supervisor polls `stop_hook_path` file-existence every 100ms; ZERO explicit alternatives. inotify/kqueue/fsevents (push, sub-ms latency, zero CPU when idle), Unix-domain-socket handshake (CLI writes 1 byte on exit), signalfd (Linus-style: child exits → SIGCHLD → signalfd readable), MCP server with subscription (hyperscaler-style: persistent connection, native to the CLI surface), or a DAP-style debug protocol over stdio — none of these are evaluated.

Settings-template language (v5 §B.3) — hand-rolled TOML chosen citing 'no serde' precedent; ZERO explicit alternatives. Build-time codegen from a Rust schema (compile-time-typechecked, no parser), CUE/Nickel/Dhall (typed config languages with built-in validation), JSON-schema-driven emitters, or Pkl (Apple's config language with first-class Rust binding) all compete on principled grounds.

Branch Y dep commitment (v4 §A.1.4) — declared as principle; v4 references prior Branch X/Z but does not preserve the comparison in the artifact. F6 cannot independently verify the rejection of `rustix` + `async_trait` was deliberated for THIS plan vs inherited from a prior round.

Capability seed file format (v4 §B.5) — hand-rolled TOML; alternative of reusing the existing JSON shape of `registry/capabilities/foundry-internal.json` is named ('flat list is simpler than the JSON shape') but the trade-off is hand-waved — emitting two formats in parallel for the same domain (TOML for supervisor, JSON for internal) is itself an F6 risk that wasn't named as a competing alternative.

Watchdog mechanism (v4 §B.3) — SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL after fixed `watchdog_secs`; alternatives like cgroup-v2 freezer (Linus-style precise control), `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG)` (parent-death auto-cleanup), or a watchdog supervisor process tree (Erlang-style) are not considered.

AccountSnapshotProvider production wiring (v4 §B.2.6 + v5 §B.4) — composite-over-3-account-adapters reading `registry/accounts/*.toml`; alternatives like a single unified `accounts.jsonl` (DRY), or a SQLite registry (queryable), or a `git`-versioned account directory with content-addressed snapshots, are not enumerated.

Drift-detection cadence (v5 §B.4) — verify-at-snapshot-time on every `tick_once`; alternatives like background-watcher (notify crate equivalent in std), CI-only check, or render-on-write-then-trust are not considered. Doing the verify on every tick (potentially many times/sec) is a perf risk that an unnamed alternative would expose.

alternatives_named: ==DECISION 1: SUPERVISOR TOPOLOGY (v4 §A.3 — author DID enumerate)==
A: Single supervisor daemon owns route→reserve→spawn→watch→settle (rejected: SPoF).
B: Per-CLI binaries with crash isolation (rejected on cost-benefit at <10msg/s).
C: In-process inside dashboard-app (rejected: layer violation).
D: Host-injected policy ports + adapter as I/O seam + kernel pure decision logic (CHOSEN).
==DECISION 2: INBOX STORAGE SUBSTRATE (v4 §B.2.4 — author did NOT enumerate; F6 supplies)==
A: JSONL on disk + hand-rolled framing + tmp→rename (THE SELECTED PATH).

B [Linus-style]: SQLite via `rusqlite` (single file, ACID guarantees free, fsync handled by SQLite, lock semantics native, hand-rolled framing eliminated). Cost: adds 1 dep (`rusqlite` ≈ 200kloc) — Branch Y violation.

C [Linus-minimalism]: Append-only segment log (BitCask-style) — fixed-record-size append + in-memory hash index + periodic compaction. Cost: still hand-rolled but with O(1) lookups and simpler crash recovery than JSONL.
D: `sled` or `redb` (Rust-native embedded KV; redb is single-file like SQLite, no C deps). Cost: 1 pure-Rust dep; redb (~70kloc) is closer to Branch Y spirit than `rusqlite`.

E [Hyperscaler-style]: NATS JetStream or Redis Streams (push-delivery, native dedup keys, native ACK semantics, replay cursors free). Cost: external service dep, blast radius >> single-file local store.
F [Hyperscaler-extreme]: Kafka-on-disk via `rdkafka` (partitioned, replayable, idempotent producer). Cost: massive over-engineering for <10msg/s foundry budget.
G: lmdb (mmap-fast read, well-tested, single file). Cost: C dep, similar trade-off to SQLite.
==DECISION 3: DEP BRANCH (v4 §A.1.4 — declared as principle; alternatives not preserved in artifact)==
Y: Zero net-new external deps; sync trait; best-effort durability (CHOSEN).
X [Linus-style]: `rustix` + `async_trait` — proper async ergonomics, syscall wrappers without `libc` macros. Cost: 2 deps, complicates the no-serde precedent.

Z [Hyperscaler-style hybrid]: Branch Y for kernel + Branch X for adapter — kernel stays zero-dep, only `oya-foundry-jsonl-supervisor-adapter` pulls in `rustix` for fsync precision. Cost: bifurcates the workspace dep policy.
==DECISION 4: SUPERVISOR↔CLI NOTIFICATION (v4 §B.3 — author did NOT enumerate; F6 supplies)==
A: Stop-hook file-existence polling at 100ms (THE SELECTED PATH).

B [Linus-style — inotify/kqueue/fsevents]: OS-native file-watcher; push-notification on path creation; sub-ms latency; zero CPU when idle. Cost: per-OS code paths; portability burden — Linux/macOS/BSD divergence. Existing Rust crate `notify` would violate Branch Y; hand-rolling is feasible but adds ~300 LOC per OS.

C [Linus-style — signalfd + SIGCHLD]: Child exits → kernel emits SIGCHLD → supervisor reads from signalfd; zero polling. Cost: Linux-only; macOS uses `kqueue EVFILT_PROC` instead. Most direct mechanism but OS-specific.

D [Linus-style — Unix-domain socket handshake]: CLI writes 1 byte to a UDS path on exit; supervisor `epoll`/`kqueue` on the socket. Cost: requires CLI to know the UDS path — same as `stop_hook_path` but with push semantics.

E [Hyperscaler-style — MCP server with subscription]: Persistent stdio connection between supervisor and CLI; MCP `notifications/progress` channel surfaces completion. Cost: requires CLI to speak MCP — Claude does (since 2024), Codex does (per `~/.codex/hooks.json`), Gemini does NOT yet. Couples to MCP runtime which is the very thing the supervisor is supposed to compose.
F [Hyperscaler-style — DAP-style debug protocol over stdio]: Bidirectional JSON-RPC; CLI sends `Stopped` event on completion. Cost: protocol design from scratch; over-engineered for a one-bit signal.

G [Linus-style — anonymous pipe + read EOF]: Spawn CLI with a pipe; supervisor blocks on `read()`; EOF (returns 0) signals completion. Cost: requires CLI to inherit the pipe FD; simplest possible mechanism if it works.
H: Reduce poll cadence (e.g. 1s) — same mechanism, lower CPU cost, higher latency. Pure tuning, not alternative architecture.
==DECISION 5: SETTINGS-TEMPLATE LANGUAGE (v5 §B.3 — author did NOT enumerate; F6 supplies)==
A: Hand-rolled TOML in adapter parser, schema mirrored in `SettingsTemplate` Rust struct (THE SELECTED PATH).

B [Linus-style — build.rs codegen from Rust schema]: `SettingsTemplate` IS the schema; build.rs emits `templates/foundry-supervisor/<provider>.toml` from a Rust constant declaration; no parser at runtime. Cost: hand-edited templates impossible; eliminates one round-trip risk.
C [Linus-minimalism — INI-style key=value]: Even simpler than TOML; trivial parser (~30 LOC). Cost: cannot express nested arrays cleanly — would force per-key escaping for hooks/skills.

D [Hyperscaler-style — CUE / Nickel / Dhall]: Typed config language with built-in validation and pure-functional semantics; provider-specific overlays expressed as record union/merge. Cost: external dep (CUE = Go binary; Nickel/Dhall = Rust-but-large); violates Branch Y. Best long-term answer if Branch Y is relaxed.
E [Hyperscaler-style — Pkl (Apple)]: Typed config language with first-class Rust binding via `pkl-rust`. Cost: 1 dep + Pkl-runtime — Branch Y violation but production-grade.
F [Hyperscaler-style — JSON Schema + Rust schemafy]: Schema-as-source-of-truth with codegen for both renderer and validator. Cost: serde dep — entire workspace policy violation.

G: TOML via the workspace's existing hand-rolled `capability-registry-app:L96` parser pattern (THE SELECTED PATH — variant of A with reuse of existing precedent). This reuse argument is valid and IS hinted at in §B.1 but not explicitly listed as a competing variant.
==DECISION 6: SETTINGS RENDERER SHAPE (v5 §A.1 — author DID enumerate, but only 2 options)==
A: Per-provider renderer adapters (Claude/Codex/Gemini) implementing one `SettingsRenderer` trait (CHOSEN).
B: Single multi-format renderer with format-flag dispatch (rejected: same anti-pattern v4 rejected for `SessionDriver`).

C [F6 SUPPLIES]: Single renderer + per-provider declarative format-descriptor (e.g. `ProviderFormatDescriptor { paths, dialect, hooks_inline_or_external, ... }` as data, not code). Cost: pushes complexity into descriptor authoring; may be cleaner than 3 renderer impls if dialects converge.
D [F6 SUPPLIES — Linus-style]: Provider-specific code-gen at build time from a single template + a per-provider format-spec; runtime renderer is a no-op. Cost: same as Decision-5-B.

E [F6 SUPPLIES — Hyperscaler-style]: Renderer-as-MCP-server — each CLI provider exposes an MCP tool `settings.apply(template)`; supervisor calls it. Couples to MCP-everywhere-already which is not yet true for Gemini.

linus_style_alternative:
INBOX: SQLite via rusqlite. One file. ACID. fsync(parent_dir) is SQLite's problem, not yours. Crash recovery is reading the file. Concurrent access is a single mutex inside SQLite. The reason every reliable local app from Firefox bookmarks to git-credential-cache uses SQLite is that it removes an entire class of bugs from your codebase. The cost is one dep — yes, a C dep, ~200kloc — but that 200kloc has been beaten on for 20 years by every device on Earth. Your hand-rolled JSONL framing is 50 lines of code that haven't been tested by anyone. Trade more dep budget for fewer bugs.
NOTIFY: anonymous pipe + read EOF. fork(), give the child the write end, close it in the parent. read() in the parent blocks until the child closes the pipe — which it does automatically on _exit(). Zero polling. Zero filesystem dance. Zero `stop_hook_path` to coordinate. This is how Unix has signaled 'I'm done' since 1973. The stop-hook touch-a-file pattern is fundamentally a workaround for the fact that the supervisor doesn't own the child's pipe — but if the supervisor IS the spawner, it DOES own the pipe.
DEP BRANCH: Branch Z hybrid. Keep the kernel zero-dep (right answer). Let the adapter pull in `rustix` for fsync precision so you can call fdatasync(parent_dir_fd) instead of best-effort prayer. The cost is one dep in one crate. The benefit is real durability semantics rather than the v4 §B.3 confession 'admit non-durability-across-power-loss'.
hyperscaler_style_alternative:
INBOX: NATS JetStream as the inbox/outbox substrate. Native dedup keys (request_id maps 1:1 to NATS message-id). Native ACK semantics replace inbox.commit/release/dead_letter — JetStream `Ack`/`Nak`/`Term` are isomorphic. Native cursor + replay. Native multi-consumer fanout (your 3 accounts × 3 providers become 9 consumer groups). Cost: external nats-server dep (~30MB Go binary) + Rust async-nats client crate. Wins: zero crash-recovery code in your repo; observability for free (Prometheus exporter built-in); supports the M03/M04 milestones when foundry exits single-host.
NOTIFY: MCP server with subscription channel. Each CLI exposes itself as an MCP server; supervisor opens persistent MCP connections; CLI emits `notifications/progress` with `{ status: 'done', message_id, tokens_in, tokens_out }` on completion. Push-delivery + structured payload + native to the protocol family the foundry is already adopting. Cost: requires CLI to speak MCP (Claude does, Codex does per ~/.codex/hooks.json, Gemini does not yet — this is the actual blocker, not the architecture).
SETTINGS-TEMPLATE: Pkl (Apple's typed config language with first-class Rust binding via pkl-rust). Typed schema + per-provider overlay + built-in validation + native lists/records. Replace hand-rolled TOML parser with `Pkl::eval(&template_pkl)`. Cost: 1 dep (pkl-rust) — Branch Y violation but real production-grade. Wins: schema evolution is checked at template-eval time, not at render-time; provider overlays compose via record merge semantics; one schema file replaces three TOML payloads + invariant-fence test + round-trip test.
DEP BRANCH: Branch X full — adopt async_trait + tokio properly. The current sync-port + spawn_blocking pool is a workaround for not committing to async. At hyperscaler scale (M04+) you'll pay this debt anyway; paying it now means the kernel design doesn't need a v2.

consensus_addendum.antithesis_steelman_against_favored_dire: The strongest counter to the 'v4+v5 ships as-is' direction is: the artifact has TWO load-bearing decisions (inbox substrate, notify mechanism) ranked at the 'silent first-solution-wins' tier without any FixupTask capturing the alternatives for revisit. Per the user's 'No silent regression (Linus-style)' principle in MEMORY.md, public-contract decisions made silently are exactly what lean-a10 BLOCKER day-1 exists to prevent. The inbox substrate IS a public contract — `InboxStore` is a kernel-published trait — and the JSONL choice locks the durability semantics that downstream µservices will inherit. Adding `ADR-foundry-jsonl-inbox-substrate` with explicit Linus/hyperscaler rejection BEFORE shipping v4 is the consistent application of the user's own no-silent-regression policy. The 'v4 is approved by Architect + Critic' status is a procedural argument, not a substantive one — the prior approval did not see the alternatives table that F6 is supplying now.
consensus_addendum.tradeoff_tension: Branch Y (zero-dep) vs Decision-Quality-Visibility. Branch Y is a STRONG, CORRECT principle for the foundry stage — it preserves audit-ability, bootstrap speed, and review surface. But Branch Y becomes a meta-anti-pattern when it ALSO functions as 'silently rejects all external alternatives without naming them'. The tension: every time Branch Y is invoked it removes an alternative from the visible options table, which IS the F6 anti-pattern. RESOLUTION: keep Branch Y as the dep policy AND require any Branch-Y-rejected alternative to be named in an ADR's 'Alternatives considered' section. This costs ~5 lines per decision and resolves the tension cleanly. The current v4/v5 does this for some decisions (renderer A vs B; topology A/B/C/D) and not others (inbox, notify, template language) — uneven application is the actual bug.
consensus_addendum.synthesis: Ship v4+v5 as-designed, BUT add 3 new ADRs (or 1 combined ADR) that name the rejected alternatives for the three silent decisions: `ADR-foundry-jsonl-inbox-substrate` (rejects SQLite/sled/redb/NATS/Kafka/lmdb with named reasons), `ADR-foundry-stop-hook-notification` (rejects inotify/signalfd/UDS/pipe-EOF/MCP/DAP with named reasons), `ADR-foundry-settings-template-language` (rejects codegen/INI/CUE/Pkl/Dhall/Nickel with named reasons). Each ADR adds 2 acceptance rows: (1) ADR exists and is grep-able for each rejected alternative name; (2) FixupTask is registered for the 'revisit-at-scale' trigger. This costs ~3 grit units (3 ADRs × ~1 unit each) and preserves the v4/v5 architecture while curing the F6 anti-pattern. The alternative — re-architecting around SQLite or inotify or Pkl — is NOT recommended at this iteration count (v5 already capped at 5 iterations per deliberate mode).
